name: Moodfit
one_liner: Self-help app for tracking mood and practising CBT thought records, breathing, gratitude journaling and daily goals.
best_for: Adults with mild to moderate low mood, stress or anxiety who want structured self-help tools
People who want to log mood alongside sleep, exercise and medication to spot patterns
People in therapy who want to track symptoms (PHQ-9, GAD-7) between sessions
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People who need diagnosis, medication or a therapist; the app is self-guided
People looking for strong evidence that an app will reduce depression: the one trial found no effect on depression scores
short_description: Moodfit is a self-guided app with a mood journal, CBT thought records, breathing and mindfulness exercises, gratitude journaling and PHQ-9/GAD-7.
long_description: Moodfit, made by Roble Ridge Software, is a self-help app for mood and stress. It includes a mood journal, CBT tools for working through negative thoughts, mindfulness and breathing exercises, a gratitude journal, daily goals, medication and activity tracking, PHQ-9 and GAD-7 questionnaires, and insights that link sleep, exercise, nutrition and social activity to your mood. The free version covers mood journaling and basic tools; Premium is a one-time purchase with no auto-renewal, listed in the App Store at $39.99 for a year, with cheaper one-year and lifetime options on Moodfit's website. In a 2026 randomized trial of 228 UK adults with mild to moderate symptoms, four weeks of Moodfit improved workplace well-being compared with a waitlist but did not significantly reduce depression scores, and the effect on anxiety was not statistically significant.
patient_summary: You log your mood and use short exercises such as CBT thought records, breathing and gratitude journaling, and the app shows how sleep, exercise and other habits relate to how you feel. The basic app is free; Premium is a one-time purchase (about $39.99 for a year in the App Store, less on the Moodfit website). It is self-help, not therapy.

pricing.starting_price: Free; Premium $39.99/year in the App Store (web plans from $19.99/year)
pricing.notes: Premium is a one-time payment with no auto-renewal. Moodfit's site lists one-year plans at $19.99–$35.99, two years for $39.99 and lifetime at $89.99–$119.99 (lifetime not sold in app stores). Refunds within 7 days. The App Store also lists $9.99 and $19.99 Premium options without stating the period.

privacy.notes: Policy says it does not sell the data you enter and keeps it encrypted on US servers; any user can email to delete it, but automatically collected usage data is kept indefinitely. The policy does not mention HIPAA.

seo.title: Moodfit: Mood Tracking + CBT App | HeyPsych
seo.meta_description: MoodFit is a mental health app combining mood tracking, CBT tools, gratitude journaling, and breathing exercises in one platform.

faqs.a: MoodFit includes mood tracking with customizable factors, CBT thought records, gratitude journaling, breathing exercises, meditation, goal tracking, and sleep logging. It's designed as an all-in-one mental wellness toolkit.
MoodFit has a free version with basic features. Premium (around $5/month) unlocks advanced analytics, additional exercises, and full feature access. The free version provides a good starting point.

MoodFit's tools are based on evidence-based approaches like CBT and gratitude practices. It's a self-help tool designed with clinical input. For diagnosable conditions, it should complement rather than replace professional treatment.

faqs.q: Can I share MoodFit data with my therapist?
faqs.a: Yes, MoodFit allows data export to share with healthcare providers. Therapists often find mood tracking data helpful for identifying patterns and adjusting treatment.

clinical_trials.study: Three-arm randomized controlled trial of Moodfit vs an executive-function training app vs waitlist in adults with mild to moderate depression and anxiety

citation.authors: MacLellan A, Fairchild G, Button KS
citation.title: The Effectiveness and Mechanisms of Action of App-Based Interventions for Improving Mental Health and Workplace Well-Being: Randomized Controlled Trial

clinical_trials.outcome: Compared with waitlist, Moodfit improved workplace well-being (UWES-9) after 4 weeks and at 12-week follow-up; no significant reduction in depression (PHQ-9); anxiety reduction at follow-up was not statistically significant. 58% attrition at follow-up.
clinical_trials.study_design: Randomized controlled trial (3 arms, waitlist control; 79 assigned to Moodfit)

primary_uses: CBT thought records for negative thinking
Tracking sleep, exercise and medication against mood
